liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (4 reviews): Track title is mislabeled, and the usual transition into I Know You Rider comes before Easy Wind; A jam links China Cat and I Know You Rider [9][10][12][13]
- **Black Peter** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds this performance wrenching; The stretch from Black Peter through New Speedway Boogie is splendid [9][14]
- **New Speedway Boogie** (2 reviews): Extended jam with a roughly three-minute outro closes the acoustic set; Features a nice jam, a favorite of the reviewer [5][6]
- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Remains intact, unlike other material split across four tracks in this copy; A cut in the recording removes much of what was likely the highlight [10][14]
- **How Long Blues** (1 review): Described as a rare song to find in the acoustic set [6]
- **El Paso** (1 review): Before this song Jerry jokes that this is where Weir gets his wish, at everyone else's expense [4]
- **Easy Wind** (1 review): The tape machine apparently wasn't running at the start, leaving only a Garcia solo and Pigpen's final verse [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **How Long Blues**: rare: 5 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-07-14.sbd.unknown.96628.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 135 min; rated 4.4/5 by 15 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound quality has issues, though they add some funny banter; lyrical slip-ups also occur; Fidelity is excellent for 1970, with some glitches and a couple of patched songs [9][13]
- **gd70-07-14.sbd.cotsman.17815.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 127 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Electric set suffers from mix problems and buzzing, while the acoustic set sounds good to this listener; A noticeable buzz runs throughout the recording [2][3]

## Around the show

- The acoustic set includes entertaining stage banter between songs [3]
- David Crosby plays 12-string guitar on Cumberland Blues and New Speedway Boogie, with Jerry on electric [12]
- David Crosby plays acoustic guitar on Cumberland Blues and New Speedway Boogie, while Garcia plays electric [2]
- The band is still playing songs from Anthem of the Sun at this point [4]
- Mellow acoustic set contrasts with a hard-rocking psychedelic electric set; old-tape sound quality is modest [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-07-14.sbd.unknown.96628.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > Master Reel > Dat> cd> shn> cd> ?> shn [1]
- **gd70-07-14.sbd.cotsman.17815.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by JCotsman; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [2]. Also: Cumberland and New Speedway may be patched in from a soundboard-to-master-reel-to-reel-to-DAT-to-CD source [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Euphoria Ballroom, San Rafael, Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1970/artwork/euphoria-ballroom-san-rafael-poster) [16]
- Poster by San Andreas Fault Grateful: [09 | December | 2017 | Original Concert Posters](https://original-concert-posters.com/2017/12/09/) [17]
